children.name: Acanthiza
children.description: The thornbills — a genus of small, active insectivores with fine, pointed bills and a habit of flicking their wings while foraging. They are the most species-rich genus in the family, occupying virtually every terrestrial habitat across Australasia. Their calls are typically high-pitched and insect-like, and their social structures range from monogamous pairs to complex cooperative groups.

children.name: Acanthiza chrysorrhoa
children.description: The yellow-rumped thornbill (Acanthiza chrysorrhoa) is a species of passerine bird from the genus Acanthiza. The genus was once placed in the family Pardalotidae but that family was split and it is now in the family Acanthizidae. There are four subspecies of yellow-rumped thornbill. It is a small, brownish bird with a distinctive yellow rump and thin dark bill. It inhabits savannah, scrub and forests across most of Australia and eats insects. The species engages in cooperative breeding.

children.name: Acanthiza lineata
children.description: The striated thornbill (Acanthiza lineata) is a species of bird in the family Acanthizidae.

children.name: Acanthiza reguloides
children.description: The buff-rumped thornbill (Acanthiza reguloides) is a small passerine bird species belonging to the genus Acanthiza, most of which are endemic to Australia. Measuring 8–10 cm in length, this unassuming thornbill is characterised by its plain greenish brown upperparts and very pale-yellow underparts, with a distinctive buff coloured rump. The tail has a broad, blackish band with a paler tip. Adults possess white irises, whilst juveniles have dark eyes. The buff-rumped thornbill is one of 14 species within the genus Acanthiza genus, which are recognisable by their thin, pointed bill. Species are unique in their plumage and distribution. Despite their shared name, the genus is not related to hummingbirds.

children.name: Acanthiza ewingii
children.description: The Tasmanian Thornbill (Acanthiza ewingii) is a small bushland member of the Acanthizidae (Australian warbler) family, endemic to Tasmania and the Bass Strait Islands.

children.name: Acanthiza herringi
children.description: A small thornbill with bold white eyebrow, found in dry woodlands of southeastern Australia.

children.name: Acanthiza iredalei
children.description:
The slender-billed thornbill (Acanthiza iredalei) is a small bird native to Australia. It includes three sub-species: * A. I. Hedleyi * A. I. Iredalei * A. I. Rosinae
This thornbill can be found in shrublands and salt marshes, typically those around salt lakes or low heath on sand plains. It eats mostly insects and spiders captured in the shrubs of its habitat. It rarely feeds on the ground, preferring instead the higher elevations of shrubs and trees.

children.name: Acanthiza robustirostris
children.description: The slaty-backed thornbill (Acanthiza robustirostris) is a species of bird in the family Acanthizidae. It is endemic to Australia.

children.name: Acanthiza inornata
children.description: The western thornbill (Acanthiza inornata) is a species of bird in the family Acanthizidae.

children.name: Acanthiza uropygialis
children.description:
The chestnut-rumped thornbill (Acanthiza uropygialis) is a small passerine bird in the family Acanthizidae, endemic to Australia.
Specially named for its pale-chestnut rump from mediaeval Latin uropygium, the rump. Its other names include chestnut-tailed or chestnut-backed thornbill, tit or tit-warbler, chestnut-rumped tit or tit-warbler. A plain, pale thornbill, with pale eyes, it is widespread throughout inland Australia, west of the Great Dividing Range to the West Australian coast but is absent in the far north and humid southwest Western Australia. It is a cooperative breeder like some of the other thornbills

children.name: Acanthiza magna
children.description: A thornbill with yellow tail from eastern Australia.

children.name: Acanthiza kelseyi
children.description: A thornbill from southwestern Australia.

children.name: Acanthornis
children.description: A monotypic genus of scrubtit from Tasmanian rainforests.

children.name: Acanthornis magna
children.description: The scrubtit (Acanthornis magna) is a species of bird in the thornbill family Acanthizidae. It is endemic to Tasmania and King Island in Australia. Its natural habitat is the temperate rainforest, Nothofagus beech forest and eucalypt woodland. It is a small species that resembles the Sericornis scrubwrens (with which it was once placed).

children.name: Aphelocephala
children.description: Small grey-brown warblers with distinctive white faces, endemic to Australia.

children.name: Aphelocephala leucopsis
children.description: The southern whiteface (Aphelocephala leucopsis) is a small passerine found in arid regions across most of the southern half of the Australian continent, excluding Tasmania.

children.name: Aphelocephala pectoralis
children.description:
The chestnut-breasted whiteface (Aphelocephala pectoralis) is a small passerine bird endemic to inland South Australia, with some unconfirmed sightings in the Northern Territory.
The species is most likely found on the Country of the Antakirinja Matu-Yankunytjatjara, Arabana and Kokatha-Barngarla peoples, although no Indigenous name has been recorded for it and Country boundaries are approximate.

children.name: Aphelocephala nigricincta
children.description: The banded whiteface (Aphelocephala nigricincta) is a species of bird in the family Acanthizidae.

children.name: Calamanthus
children.description: Small, ground-dwelling warblers with finely streaked plumage, endemic to Australia.

children.name: Calamanthus fuliginosus
children.description: The striated fieldwren (Calamanthus fuliginosus) is a species of bird in the family Acanthizidae, endemic to Australia.

children.name: Calamanthus campestris
children.description: The rufous fieldwren (Calamanthus campestris) also known as the desert wren or sandplain wren is a species of insectivorous bird in the family Acanthizidae, endemic to Australia.

children.name: Cincloramphus
children.description: A genus of large, grassland-dwelling warblers found across Australasia and the Pacific. They are robust, streaky birds with strong legs, adapted for a terrestrial lifestyle in open habitats. Their songs are often loud and complex, delivered from exposed perches or in flight.

children.name: Cincloramphus cruralis
children.description: The brown songlark (Cincloramphus cruralis), also Australian songlark, is a small passerine bird found throughout much of Australia.

children.name: Cincloramphus timoriensis
children.description: The tawny grassbird (Cincloramphus timoriensis) is a large songbird that is a member of the family Locustellidae commonly found in grassland and reedbed habitats.

children.name: Cincloramphus mathewsi
children.description: The rufous songlark (Cincloramphus mathewsi) is a species in the family Locustellidae endemic to Australia.

children.name: Cincloramphus macrurus
children.description: The Papuan grassbird (Cincloramphus macrurus) is a species of typical grassbird in the family Locustellidae.

children.name: Gerygone
children.description: The gerygones — a genus of small, insectivorous warblers found from Southeast Asia through Australasia to the Pacific islands. They are active, acrobatic foragers with fine, pointed bills and often brightly coloured facial patterns. Many species are known for their distinctive, descending songs, which give them their common name 'flyeaters'.

children.name: Gerygone albogularis
children.description:
The white-throated gerygone (Gerygone olivacea) is a species of bird in the family Acanthizidae. It is found in Australia and Papua New Guinea. Its natural habitats are temperate forests and subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests. Its common names include white-throated warbler, white-throated flyeater, bush canary, and native canary.
Gerygone comes from the Greek word "gerugonos" meaning "echos". The species name olivacea is latin for 'olive-green', given for its underbelly coloration.

children.name: Gerygone caledonica
children.description: A gerygone from New Caledonia.

children.name: Gerygone chloronota
children.description: The green-backed gerygone (Gerygone chloronota) is a species of bird in the family Acanthizidae found in northern Australia and New Guinea. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests and subtropical or tropical mangrove forests.

children.name: Gerygone chrysocras
children.description: A small warbler with bright yellow underparts, found in New Guinea.

children.name: Gerygone chrysogaster
children.description: The yellow-bellied gerygone is a species of bird in the family Acanthizidae. The Yellow-Bellied Gerygone is native to New Guinea, typically found in subtropical or tropical moist lowlands forest. Shown to have least concern about population with it being very common, but is currently decreasing in population throughout New Guinea.

children.name: Gerygone cinerea
children.description: The grey thornbill, ashy gerygone or mountain gerygone (Acanthiza cinerea) is a species of bird in the family Acanthizidae.

children.name: Gerygone dorsalis
children.description: The rufous-sided gerygone is a species of bird in the family Acanthizidae. It is found in the eastern Lesser Sunda Islands and Kai Islands.

children.name: Gerygone flavolateralis
children.description: The fan-tailed gerygone is a species of bird in the family Acanthizidae. It is found in New Caledonia and Vanuatu. The Rennell gerygone of the Solomon Islands was formerly considered conspecific, but was split as a distinct species by the IOC in 2021.

children.name: Gerygone fusca
children.description: The western gerygone (Gerygone fusca) is a small, brownish-grey species of passerine bird, which is found in inland and south-west Australia.

children.name: Gerygone igata
children.description: The grey warbler (Gerygone igata), also known by its Māori name or outside New Zealand as the grey gerygone, is an insectivorous bird in the family Acanthizidae endemic to New Zealand.

children.name: Gerygone inornata
children.description: The plain gerygone is a species of bird in the family Acanthizidae. It is found on the islands of Wetar and Timor. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical mangrove forest.

children.name: Gerygone lateralis
children.description: Gerygone lateralis (Gerygone) is a australasian warblers species found in Asia region.

children.name: Gerygone levigaster
children.description: The mangrove gerygone (Gerygone levigaster) is a species of bird in the Australian warbler family Acanthizidae.

children.name: Gerygone magnirostris
children.description: The large-billed gerygone (Gerygone magnirostris) is a species of bird in the family Acanthizidae found in northern Australia and New Guinea.

children.name: Gerygone modesta
children.description: The Norfolk gerygone is a species of bird in the Australian warbler family Acanthizidae. It is endemic to Norfolk Island. This species was once lumped with the grey gerygone of New Zealand and the extinct Lord Howe gerygone as a single species.

children.name: Gerygone mouki
children.description: The brown gerygone (Gerygone mouki), previously known as the brown warbler, is a small passerine bird native to eastern coastal Australia.

children.name: Gerygone olivacea
children.description:
The white-throated gerygone (Gerygone olivacea) is a species of bird in the family Acanthizidae. It is found in Australia and Papua New Guinea. Its natural habitats are temperate forests and subtropical or tropical moist lowland forests. Its common names include white-throated warbler, white-throated flyeater, bush canary, and native canary.
Gerygone comes from the Greek word "gerugonos" meaning "echos". The species name olivacea is latin for 'olive-green', given for its underbelly coloration.

children.name: Gerygone palpebrosa
children.description: The fairy gerygone (Gerygone palpebrosa), previously known as the fairy warbler, is a species of bird in the family Acanthizidae native to New Guinea and Queensland.

children.name: Gerygone ruficollis
children.description: The brown-breasted gerygone or treefern gerygone (Gerygone ruficollis) is a species of bird in the family Acanthizidae. It is found in the highlands of New Guinea. Its natural habitat is subtropical or tropical moist montane forests.

children.name: Gerygone sulphurea
children.description: The golden-bellied gerygone (Gerygone sulphurea) is a species of bird in the family Acanthizidae. It is found in Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Cambodia, Vietnam and Thailand. Its natural habitats are subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest and subtropical or tropical mangrove forest.

children.name: Gerygone tenebrosa
children.description: The dusky gerygone (Gerygone tenebrosa) is a species of bird in the family Acanthizidae.

children.name: Hylacola
children.description: Small secretive warblers with rufous rumps, endemic to southern Australia.

children.name: Hylacola cauta
children.description: The shy heathwren (Hylacola cauta) is a species of small bird in the family Acanthizidae, endemic to Australia.

children.name: Hylacola pyrrhopygia
children.description: The chestnut-rumped heathwren (Hylacola pyrrhopygia) is a species of bird in the family Acanthizidae. It is endemic to temperate and subtropical forests and heathlands of Australia.

children.name: Oreoscopus
children.description: A monotypic genus of fernwren from Queensland rainforests.

children.name: Oreoscopus gutturalis
children.description:
The fernwren (Oreoscopus gutturalis) is a species of bird in the family Acanthizidae. It is monotypic within the genus Oreoscopus.
It is endemic to northern Queensland in Australia. Its natural habitats are tropical moist lowland forest and tropical moist montane forest.

children.name: Origma
children.description: Small active warblers of rocky habitats in Australia and New Guinea.

children.name: Origma solitaria
children.description: The rockwarbler (Origma solitaria), is a bird in the family Acanthizidae. It is the only bird species endemic to the mainland of the state of New South Wales in Australia.

children.name: Origma rufogularis
children.description: A small warbler with rufous throat, found in rocky hills of southern New Guinea.

children.name: Pachycare
children.description: A monotypic genus of goldenface from the montane forests of New Guinea.

children.name: Pachycare flavogrisea
children.description: The goldenface (Pachycare flavogriseum) is a species of passerine bird endemic to New Guinea. It is the only species (monotypic) within the genus Pachycare.

children.name: Poodytes
children.description: A genus of small, secretive grass-dwelling warblers endemic to Australia and New Zealand. They are skulking birds of dense grassland and swamp vegetation, with short tails and strong legs adapted for a terrestrial lifestyle.

children.name: Poodytes gramineus
children.description: The little grassbird (Poodytes gramineus) is a species of Old World warbler in the family Locustellidae.

children.name: Poodytes carteri
children.description: The spinifexbird (Poodytes carteri) is endemic to inland Australia. Also known as Carter's desertbird, it is named after Thomas Carter, an English ornithologist and pastoralist active in Western Australia from 1887 to 1928.

children.name: Poodytes punctatus
children.description: The New Zealand fernbird or simply fernbird (Poodytes punctatus) is an insectivorous bird endemic to New Zealand. In the Māori language, it is named kōtātā or mātātā.

children.name: Poodytes rufescens
children.description: The Chatham Islands fernbird (Poodytes rufescens) is an extinct bird species that was endemic to the Chatham Islands. It was historically known only from Mangere Island, but fossils have been found on Pitt Island and Chatham Island as well. Its closest living relative is the New Zealand fernbird or matata (Poodytes punctatus). It was formerly treated as a subspecies of the New Zealand fernbird, but is now widely recognized as its own species. Both fernbirds were formerly placed in their own genus Bowdleria; they were later moved to Megalurus and most recently Poodytes.

children.name: Pyrrholaemus
children.description: Small ground-dwelling warblers with red-brown throats, endemic to Australia.

children.name: Pyrrholaemus brunneus
children.description: The redthroat (Pyrrholaemus brunneus) is a small, mostly ground-dwelling species of bird in the family Acanthizidae. It is endemic to Australia, occurring mostly in arid and semi-arid areas containing acacia and chenopod shrublands. The species has a distinctive red throat patch and is able to mimic the calls of numerous other bird species.

children.name: Pyrrholaemus sagittatus
children.description: The speckled warbler (Pyrrholaemus sagittatus) is a species of bird in the family Acanthizidae.

children.name: Sericornis
children.description: The scrubwrens — a genus of secretive, primarily ground-dwelling warblers with a furtive, mouse-like behaviour, found in the densest parts of forests and heathlands. They have short, rounded wings and strong legs, and their plumage is typically a rich blend of browns, olive-greens, and rufous. Most species are restricted to Australia and New Guinea.

children.name: Sericornis frontalis
children.description:
The white-browed scrubwren (Sericornis frontalis) is a passerine bird found on the New England Tablelands and coastal areas of Australia. Placed in the family Pardalotidae in the Sibley-Ahlquist taxonomy, this has met with opposition and indeed is now known to be wrong; they rather belong to the independent family Acanthizidae.
It is insectivorous and inhabits undergrowth, from which it rarely ventures, though can be found close to urban areas. It is long and predominantly brown in colour with prominent white brows and pale eyes, though the three individual subspecies vary widely. Found in small groups, it is sedentary and engages in cooperative breeding. The larger Tasmanian scrubwren was formerly considered a subspecies of this species.

children.name: Sericornis humilis
children.description: The Tasmanian scrubwren or brown scrubwren (Sericornis humilis) is a bird species endemic to the temperate forests of Tasmania and nearby King Island.

children.name: Sericornis citreogularis
children.description:
The yellow-throated scrubwren (Neosericornis citreogularis) is a passerine in the family Acanthizidae that is found in parts of eastern coastal Australia. It was formerly placed in the genus Sericornis, but is now the only species in the genus Neosericornis.
A small ground-dwelling bird that inhabits wet forest or rainforest, it is mainly insectivorous. The bird has a distinctive yellow throat and eyebrow. The male face is black and the female brown. The crown and upperparts are dark- to olive-brown, and the underparts cream, white or washed-out olive. The wings are dark brown and edged with yellow. Breeding twice or more in a long breeding season, it nests in large, suspended, pear-shaped structures. Often over water, they resemble flood debris, which they are often placed nearby. These nests are the preferred roosts of the golden-tipped bat (Phoniscus papuensis).

children.name: Sericornis magnirostris
children.description: The large-billed scrubwren (Sericornis magnirostra) is a passerine bird in the family Acanthizidae, endemic to eastern Australia. It is found in denser undergrowth in temperate forest, subtropical or tropical moist lowland forest, and subtropical or tropical moist montane forest.

children.name: Sericornis beccarii
children.description: The tropical scrubwren or Beccari's scrubwren (Sericornis beccarii) is a bird species.

children.name: Sericornis novaeguineae
children.description: A large scrubwren found in the montane forests of New Guinea.

children.name: Sericornis rufescens
children.description: The Vogelkop scrubwren (Aethomyias rufescens) is a bird species in the family Acanthizidae.

children.name: Smicrornis
children.description: A monotypic genus containing the Weebill, which at 8–9 cm is one of the smallest birds in Australia. It is a compact, active insectivore with a short tail, a pale, slightly curved bill, and a persistent, loud call that seems far too big for such a tiny bird. It is common across much of the continent in dry forests and woodlands.

children.name: Smicrornis brevirostris
children.description: The weebill (Smicrornis brevirostris) is a species of bird in the family Acanthizidae. It is an insectivorous passerine that is found throughout mainland Australia. At long, it is Australia's smallest bird. It was originally described by John Gould in 1838, and four subspecies are recognised. The weebill's plumage is nondescript, with olive-grey upperparts and paler, more yellowish underparts. It grades from more brownish plumage in the southern regions of Australia to more yellow in tropical areas.
